chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I work in some of my estates until I sweat, although there are those who can suffice for me, so that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, may know that I seek the permissible livelihood.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams work with their own hands despite having wealth and servants?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) illustrates the principle of *ittiba'* (emulation) by personally engaging in manual labor in his estates, not out of necessity, but to visibly demonstrate the pursuit of *rizq al-halal*. This act underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis that leadership and spiritual authority do not exempt one from the dignity of work, serving as a practical model for the community to avoid idleness and reliance on others when capable. It highlights the spiritual merit of self-sufficiency and the intention (*niyyah*) behind earning a livelihood as an act of worship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> tend to work in a site of mine<sup>asws</sup> until I<sup>asws</sup> sweat, altthough there are for me<sup>asws</sup> ones who can suffice for me<sup>asws</sup>, in order for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> to Know that I<sup>asws</sup> seek the Permissible livelihood’.
en.sarwar: 15. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir from who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, T work in a certain site of my work to perspire, even though there are people who can do all the work instead of me but I work so Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, finds me striving to find lawful sustenance.’”
